title: Optimal Two-Qubit Gate-Cutting Cost and Measures of Nonlocality
abstract: Circuit cutting enables quantum computations to be decomposed into smaller subcircuits at the cost of additional sampling overhead. Gate-cutting provides one such approach by replacing nonlocal gates with quasiprobability decompositions of local operations. Starting from the known optimal two-qubit gate-cutting formula, we derive complete sharp lower and upper envelopes relating the quasiprobability extent $γ$ to five established descriptors: entangling power, gate typicality, operator entanglement, Schmidt strength, and maximum product-input concurrence. We recast $γ$ as a Rényi-$1/2$ functional of the operator-Schmidt spectrum and show how the physical constraints on two-qubit spectra sharpen generic entropy bounds and select a small set of recurring extremal Cartan families. None of the five descriptors generically determines $γ$ alone, but each imposes exact constraints, revealing how substantially the optimal gate-cutting cost can vary between gates with similar nonlocal characteristics.

bite.hook: We derive complete sharp lower and outer envelopes relating quasiprobability extent to five nonlocality descriptors.
tldr: Derived complete sharp lower and upper envelopes linking the quasiprobability extent to five established nonlocality descriptors.
Recast the extent as a Rényi-1/2 functional of the operator-Schmidt spectrum.
Showed that optimal gate-cutting cost can vary significantly between gates with similar nonlocal characteristics.
bite.whyItMatters: Circuit cutting allows running large quantum algorithms on smaller quantum computers, and optimizing this cost makes hybrid computing practical.
bite.eli5: If you need to chop a complex puzzle into smaller pieces to solve it on tiny desks, knowing the exact cost of each cut helps you waste the least amount of time and effort.

glossary.shortDef: A technique to simulate larger quantum circuits by splitting them into smaller pieces using classical post-processing.
glossary.eli5Def: Cutting a massive quantum puzzle into bite-sized pieces so small computers can solve them.

glossary.shortDef: A measure of the overhead required to simulate non-positive quasiprobability distributions.
glossary.eli5Def: A penalty score that tells you how much extra computational work you have to do when chopping up quantum gates.

glossary.shortDef: The ability of a quantum operation to generate entanglement from product states.
glossary.eli5Def: A rating of how good a gate is at tying quantum particles together in spooky sync.
